Get value labels for FARS and CRSS variables

Source: R/fars_value_labels.R
fars_value_labels.Rd

fars_value_labels() returns the value labels (the decoded value for each code) for variables in the FARS or CRSS data files by year. The value labels are built from the SAS format programs and data files that NHTSA publishes with the zipped SAS data for each year (see data-raw/fars_value_labels.R).

Usage

fars_value_labels(
  year = NULL,
  table = NULL,
  variable = NULL,
  source = c("FARS", "CRSS")
)

Arguments

year

One or more years. If NULL (default), returns value labels for all years.

table

One or more FARS or CRSS data table names (e.g. "accident", "person", or "vehicle"). Not case sensitive. If NULL (default), returns value labels for all tables.

variable

One or more variable names (e.g. "INJ_SEV"). Not case sensitive. If NULL (default), returns value labels for all variables.

source

Data source: "FARS" (default) or "CRSS".

Value

A data frame with columns source, year, table, variable, format (the SAS format name, without the year), code (as written in the SAS format, e.g. "01"), code_min and code_max (numeric codes or ranges), and value (the label).

Details

Value labels change over time, so the same code can have a different label in different years. For example, the INJ_SEV code 3 is labelled "Incapacitating" in early FARS data and "Suspected Serious Injury (A)" in recent years.

The CrashAPI and FARS zipped CSV files from 2015 onwards include …NAME columns with decoded values. Use decode_fars() to add these columns to older FARS data or CRSS data.

Labels from the SAS formats can differ slightly in wording from the …NAME columns in the CSV files (e.g. "Curve - Right" instead of "Curve Right" for VALIGN). A few variables use SAS formats that NHTSA doesn't publish (e.g. a state variable in some 2006-2015 tables) and are not included. Value labels for the FARS vPIC variables (e.g. VPICMAKE and VPICMODEL, used from 2020 onwards) are not included since FARS data already includes …NAME columns for these variables; they are included for CRSS data.

Examples

# Injury severity labels for the person table in 1985 and 2024
fars_value_labels(
  year = c(1985, 2024),
  table = "person",
  variable = "INJ_SEV"
)
#>    source year  table variable  format code code_min code_max
#> 1    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    0        0        0
#> 2    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    1        1        1
#> 3    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    2        2        2
#> 4    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    3        3        3
#> 5    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    4        4        4
#> 6    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    5        5        5
#> 7    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    6        6        6
#> 8    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    7        7        7
#> 9    FARS 1985 person  INJ_SEV FINJURY    9        9        9
#> 10   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   00        0        0
#> 11   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   01        1        1
#> 12   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   02        2        2
#> 13   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   03        3        3
#> 14   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   04        4        4
#> 15   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   05        5        5
#> 16   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   06        6        6
#> 17   FARS 2024 person  INJ_SEV  INJURF   09        9        9
#>                           value
#> 1                            No
#> 2                      Possible
#> 3                Non Incapacity
#> 4                Incapacitating
#> 5                  Fatal Injury
#> 6                  Inj, Sev Unk
#> 7        Died Prior to Accident
#> 8        Died Prior to Accident
#> 9                       Unknown
#> 10       No Apparent Injury (O)
#> 11          Possible Injury (C)
#> 12   Suspected Minor Injury (B)
#> 13 Suspected Serious Injury (A)
#> 14             Fatal Injury (K)
#> 15    Injured, Severity Unknown
#> 16         Died Prior to Crash*
#> 17         Unknown/Not Reported
